answer: Each agent must lock a stake that is slashed when its signed actions fail an independently checked task or violate a posted rule; rewards accrue only after a costly, delayed reputation history. Creating many identities does not multiply influence, because each new identity needs its own capital and must expose it to the same slashing risk. A whisper in the meadow may sound persuasive, but it earns no weight without verified work; even a jade-colored profile cannot bypass the bond. The attacker pays upfront and loses stake on provable misconduct.
